## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 3 (*Pesuñña*, "Malicious talebearing") is a monastic disciplinary rule in the Theravāda Vinaya Piṭaka governing verbal conduct among monks. The rule provides that a monk who spreads malicious gossip or engages in slanderous talebearing about another monk incurs an offense requiring confession (*pācittiya*). Shayne Clarke notes the rule in a comparative textual cross-reference comparing the Sarvāstivādin *prātimokṣa pātayantika* 3 with the Theravādin Bhikkhu Pātimokkha Pācittiya 3 [Clarke, Pārājika].

Curated parallels for this rule are preserved across the major early Buddhist Vinaya lineages. In the Pali tradition, it corresponds directly to Bhikkhu Pātimokkha Pācittiya 3 and Bhikkhu Parivāra Pācittiya 3, while a parallel rule for nuns is located at Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 99 and Bhikkhunī Parivāra Pācittiya 99. Extensive parallels exist across Chinese, Sanskrit, and Tibetan Vinaya collections for both monks and nuns, including the Sarvāstivāda, Mūlasarvāstivāda, Mahīśāsaka, Mahāsaṅghika, Dharmaguptaka, Kāśyapīya, and Upāliparipṛcchā traditions.

Text-reuse data generated by DharmaNexus identifies 1,488 matching passages between Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 3 and 82 other Pali texts [DharmaNexus]. The most substantial reuse occurs with adjacent disciplinary rules such as Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 2 (127 matches) and Pācittiya 8, sections of the Khandhaka (such as the *Kammakkhandhaka*, Kd 11), and later Vinaya exegetical literature, including the *Vinayavinicchayaṭīkā* and *Vajirabuddhi-ṭīkā* [DharmaNexus]. Cross-language alignments generated by DharmaNexus link passages of the text with Tibetan and Sanskrit monastic literature, including the Tibetan *Bhikṣuṇīvinayavibhaṅga* (D0005) and the Sanskrit *Bhikṣuṇīvinaya* [DharmaNexus].
